evidence:
Source-audit findings (read-only reading of the repositories; each item was verified in code by an analyst unless marked docs-only).

PAPERCLIP (paperclipai/paperclip @ bd203093, TypeScript):
- LICENSE file: MIT License, Copyright (c) 2025 Paperclip AI. All 40 package.json files that declare a license say MIT.
- Agents are rows in an agents table with name, role (ceo/cto/engineer/...), title, status (active/paused/idle/running/error/pending_approval/terminated), adapter configuration and API keys. Per-agent runtime state (session id, token and cost totals) persists across runs in agent_runtime_state and agent_task_sessions. Each agent is executed by launching a third-party CLI (Claude Code, Codex, Grok Build, etc.).
- agents.reports_to references another agent; a cycle check and same-company check exist; an org chart API exists; a broken reporting chain blocks invocation. There is no department entity. Any standard agent may assign tasks to any agent in the company, not only subordinates.
- budget_policies table with scope company, agent or project; metric billed_cents only; soft warning at 80 percent; hard stop auto-pauses the scope and creates a budget_override_required approval. Cost is recorded when a run ends; runs billed by subscription record 0 cents.
- goals table with parent_id tree and level (company/team/agent/task). issues carry one goal_id, defaulted from the project or the company root goal. Agents receive at most one goal (id, title, level, parent id) and only when they call a heartbeat-context API; the goal tree is not walked for them. Generic child-issue creation does not inherit the parent's goal.
- Heartbeat runs: timer, assignment, on-demand and automation wakes; a durable wake-request queue with coalescing; heartbeat_runs rows; a 60-second controller lease; an orphan reaper marks dead runs process_lost.
- Task checkout is a single compare-and-swap UPDATE on the issue that sets the executing run; stale checkouts are adopted under SELECT FOR UPDATE; blocks-type dependencies between issues gate checkout; issue-creation deduplication uses advisory locks. There is no time-to-live lease on the task itself.
- Approvals table with states pending, revision_requested, approved, rejected, cancelled; only board users can approve or reject (enforced server-side). Hire approval is off by default since migration 0071. Agent-created strategy approvals are advisory: nothing stops the agent acting before approval. In the default local_trusted deployment mode, any HTTP request without a bearer token is treated as the board with instance-admin rights.
- Every business table has company_id; 573 route-level access-check calls guard 862 route handlers; agent JWTs are signed with a per-company derived key; cross-tenant route tests exist. There is no Postgres row-level security and core foreign keys are not composite with company_id. Project docs describe the product as 'single-tenant deployment, multi-company data model'.
- activity_log records actor, action, entity, run, API key and responsible user at 536 call sites. Rows are hard-deleted when an agent or company is deleted; no database protection against UPDATE or DELETE exists. The README says 'immutable audit log' (docs-only claim).

GROK BUILD (xai-org/grok-build @ f0e3be11, Rust):
- LICENSE file: Apache License 2.0 text preceded by 'Copyright 2023-2026 SpaceXAI'. All 98 first-party crates declare Apache-2.0. A THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES file (18,925 lines) exists, but 255 locked package versions from Cargo.lock have no entry in it. Three NOTICE-type files exist under third_party/ and two ratatui crates.
- Rust 2024 workspace of about 100 crates on toolchain 1.94. The agent runtime (MvpAgent, SessionActor) runs on tokio. 'grok -p' runs a single headless turn with plain, json, streaming-json and streaming-messages-json output, --json-schema structured output and exit codes 0/1/130/143. 'grok agent stdio' and 'grok agent serve' run the agent headlessly over ACP.
- Implements Agent Client Protocol V1 (agent-client-protocol crate 0.10.4) on both agent and client sides, plus about 100 x.ai/* extension methods.
- MCP client via rmcp: stdio and streamable HTTP transports, OAuth for MCP servers, project and global scope, liveness checks. Plugins: Claude-compatible plugin.json manifests with skills, commands, agents, hooks and MCP servers, local and git marketplaces; manifests declare no permissions and there are no signatures.
- Sandbox crate uses Seatbelt on macOS and Landlock, seccomp and bubblewrap on Linux, with profiles workspace, devbox, read-only, strict and custom. The default is off; if the kernel refuses, it logs and continues without a sandbox; child network blocking works on Linux only; no Windows support, containers, VMs or CPU/memory/disk limits.
- Custom models: [model.*] and [model_providers.*] config entries set base_url, api_key or env_key, headers and one of three wire protocols (OpenAI Chat Completions, OpenAI Responses, Anthropic Messages). Model discovery is a single configurable GET {base}/models endpoint; parsed capability fields cover context window and reasoning effort but not vision, tools, pricing or rate limits. Requests carry x-grok-* headers. No provider failover.
- Authentication: browser OAuth Authorization Code with PKCE S256 and loopback redirect against auth.x.ai or one configured customer OIDC issuer (discovery, JWKS-verified id_token, nonce); RFC 8628 device flow with hard-coded xAI endpoint paths; external auth provider = a configured command whose stdout is a token (session-level and per-model); API keys via XAI_API_KEY and per-model api_key/env_key. Tokens are stored in plaintext ~/.grok/auth.json with 0600 permissions; no OS keychain.
- Subagents: GROK_SUBAGENTS environment variable enables (1) or disables (0) the spawn_subagent tool; it is on by default. Subagents are in-process child sessions on separate threads, default depth limit 1, up to 32 concurrent per session, optional git-worktree isolation. There are no task leases, no dependency graph and no out-of-process worker processes.

claims.text: Paperclip is MIT-licensed.
Paperclip treats agents as persistent company employees.
Paperclip models an agent hierarchy.
Paperclip has budgets for agents.
In Paperclip, every task traces back to company goals and agents understand the goal ancestry of their work.
Paperclip has agent heartbeats.
Paperclip coordinates tasks between agents so that two agents do not work the same task at once.
Paperclip enforces governance so that the human board must approve governed actions before agents can take them.
Paperclip enforces company isolation between companies.
Paperclip keeps an immutable audit trail.
Grok Build's first-party code is Apache-2.0 with additional third-party notices.
Grok Build has a native Rust runtime with headless execution.
Grok Build supports ACP (Agent Client Protocol).
Grok Build supports MCP and plugins.
Grok Build sandboxes agent execution.
Grok Build supports custom models at custom endpoints.
Grok Build can discover models from custom model endpoints.
Grok Build supports browser authentication.
Grok Build supports device authorization.
Grok Build supports OIDC.
Grok Build supports external auth providers.
Grok Build supports API-key credentials.
Grok Build's GROK_SUBAGENTS feature shows it already has an agent-worker architecture that an orchestrator could use.
